name: India

choices.ceiling: 12% of the ₹15,000 wage ceiling (₹1,800 a month)
choices.basic: 12% of basic pay (taken as 50% of salary)

items.label: Taxable income
items.note: After the ₹75,000 standard deduction for salaried employees.

items.label: Tax at slab rates
items.note: New regime slabs. The section 87A rebate removes the tax entirely up to ₹12 lakh of taxable income, and marginal relief caps it at the income above ₹12 lakh just beyond that.

items.label: Surcharge
items.note: 10% of tax above ₹50 lakh, 15% above ₹1 crore and 25% above ₹2 crore, with marginal relief at each step.

items.label: Income tax and surcharge
items.note: New tax regime (the default): nothing to ₹4 lakh, then 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25% in steps of ₹4 lakh, and 30% above ₹24 lakh.

items.label: Employees' Provident Fund (EPF)
items.note: The employee's 12% share, either on the statutory ₹15,000-a-month wage ceiling or on full basic pay, taken here as half of salary (the minimum the 2025 labour codes allow wages to be). No tax relief under the new regime.

items.label: Professional tax
items.note: ₹2,500 a year — ₹200 a month and ₹300 in one month — the maximum the Constitution allows (Article 276). Maharashtra charges it on pay over ₹10,000 a month, Karnataka on pay of ₹25,000 a month or more.

assumptions: Resident individual under 60 on the new tax regime
notModelled: The old tax regime and its deductions (80C, HRA, home loan interest)
Professional tax in states other than Maharashtra and Karnataka, and Maharashtra's lower slabs below ₹10,000 a month and exemptions for women
provisional: Rates come from secondary sources that agree the 2026 Budget left the new-regime slabs unchanged under the Income Tax Act 2025
Professional tax thresholds for Maharashtra and Karnataka come from payroll references, not the state notifications
